text.p: Following are the main stories in Slovenia's Tuesday morning newspapers:

- Former communist party, the United List of Social Democrats, on Monday introduced its own proposal for a referendum where it would be decided whether to limit the amount of forest areas, nationalised after World War Two, that could be returned to their previous owners.
Two other political parties have pushed for a similar referendum but the three parties so far failed to agree on the maximum amount of forests that could be returned.

- Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi arrived on his first official visit to Slovenia late on Monday. Talks with his Slovenian counterpart Janez Drnovsek will focus on Slovenia's bid for NATO and EU membership and on economic cooperation between the two countries.
- Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek met representatives of Slovenian minorities in Italy and Italian minorities in Slovenia on Monday. Talks showed relations between the two countries were good.
- Three deputy mayors of Maribor, Slovenia's second largest city, resigned on Monday over salary disputes with mayor Alojz Krizman.
- From April, car insurance premiums for drivers of up to 25 years of age will be raised 35 percent as young drivers cause the majority of traffic accidents in Slovenia.

- Representatives of Austria and Slovenia on Monday signed a social agreement which determines benefits for citizens of both countries who work in neighbouring Austria or Slovenia. The previous agreement expired at the beginning of this year.
